record.original_question: For the Kuramoto-type global synchronization notion where a graph is globally synchronizing when all local minima of E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) are global minima at constant phases, is the following extremal statement true: for every epsilon > 0 there exists n and an n-vertex graph G with minimum degree at least (3/4 - epsilon)n that is not globally synchronizing?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5 (Density threshold for Global Synchrony). For any ε > 0, there exists n > 0 and a graph G on n nodes such that the minimum degree of G is at least (3/4 - ε)n and G is not globally synchronizing.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A=(A_{ij})$. To each vertex $i\in V$ assign a phase $\theta_i\in\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, and define the Kuramoto energy
$$E(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)=\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}A_{ij}\bigl(1-\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)\bigr).$$
A constant-phase configuration is one in which $\theta_1=\theta_2=\cdots=\theta_n$; these are the global minima of $E$ (with value $0$). The graph $G$ is said to be globally synchronizing if every local minimum of $E$ is a constant-phase configuration (equivalently, a global minimum).

Decide whether the following statement is true:

For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist an integer $n\ge 1$ and an $n$-vertex graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge(\tfrac{3}{4}-\varepsilon)n$ such that $G$ is not globally synchronizing.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture concerns the sharp minimum-degree threshold μ_c for global synchronization of Kuramoto networks. Kassabov, Strogatz and Townsend (2021) proved every graph with minimum degree ≥ 0.75(n−1) is globally synchronizing, giving μ_c ≤ 3/4, and argued that linear stability analysis cannot improve this. The matching lower bound — i.e., the existence, for every ε>0, of graphs of minimum degree ≥ (3/4−ε)n that are not globally synchronizing — remains conjectural and unproven as of recent work (e.g., 2025 papers on expander and threshold graphs).

status_evidence.title: Sufficiently dense Kuramoto networks are globally synchronizing
status_evidence.snippet: Networks where each oscillator is coupled to at least μ(n-1) others; proves μ_c ≤ 3/4 and discusses that this is the best obtainable from linear stability analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound μ_c ≤ 3/4 is established; matching lower bound is conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Expander graphs are globally synchronizing
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the conjectured threshold 3/4 for global synchronization of Kuramoto oscillators on graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The exact value of the critical density and the existence of dense non-synchronizing graphs near 3/4 remain open.

status_evidence.title: Threshold Graphs are Globally Synchronizing
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on global synchronization on graphs; the 3/4 density conjecture is referenced as still open.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open in the literature as of 2025.
